# Trader Fair-Bet Probability and Number Sequences

[← Akuna Capital](../README.md) · [Every Akuna Capital question](../../akuna-capital.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/trader-fair-bet-probability-and-number-sequences)

`math` `math-reasoning` `probability` `verbal`

---

## Requirements

The trader-oriented OA expects quick numerical responses rather than lengthy reasoning.

Basic fair-bet setup:

> For every event, suppose you may wager an amount that pays back `1000` together with your initial stake when the event happens. Provide the dollar stake that gives the wager an expected value of exactly zero, rounded to the nearest dollar.

Typical probability events include:

- Draw a card and win when it is a face card or an ace.
- Draw one marble from 20, consisting of 11 green and 9 blue marbles, and win on green.
- Select an hour at random and win if it falls from 9 AM through 5 PM.
- Flip a coin two or four times and win for two heads, at least one head, or the precise sequence heads followed by tails.
- Roll dice and win when the result is not a 6, is odd, or has two-dice sum equal to 12.
- Select a day at random from February 2025 and win if it is a weekday.
- Select a random four-digit number and win when its final two digits are `00`.

Sequence problems cover geometric progressions, alternating calculations, fractional sequences, alphabet-based patterns, look-and-say-like strings, and series combining sign and magnitude changes.

## Notes

With win probability `p` and stake `s`, set the expected value to zero as follows:

```
p * 1000 - (1 - p) * s = 0
s = 1000p / (1 - p)
```

Some candidates describe the payout another way; in the displayed prompt, the returned sum is `1000` plus the initial stake, meaning a win produces net profit of `1000` while a loss costs the stake.

Speed is the main constraint. Commit familiar fractions and their fair-stake equivalents to memory: `1/2 -> 1000`, `1/3 -> 500`, `1/4 -> 333`, `1/5 -> 250`, `2/3 -> 2000`, `3/4 -> 3000`, `5/6 -> 5000`.

## Preparation

- Practice eight-minute mental-arithmetic sets; ordinary Zetamac drills are useful but may not include the larger-number format.
- Turn standard card, dice, coin, calendar, and spinner probabilities into fair stakes without having to write the equation every time.
- For sequences, identify the category first: arithmetic or geometric, alternating subsequences, numerators and denominators independently, alphabet positions, or recursive digit descriptions.
